correctness.rationale: For r>=3, independent vertex sets lie inside one part; a TOIDS is exactly a set whose complement lies in one part, since it contains every vertex of at least two other parts and is automatically total dominating. In a two-block partition neither block may be pure in one part, and subtracting each unique forbidden pure block from the 2^(N-1)-1 unordered nonempty bipartitions gives c2. With three coalition blocks, at least two complement classes must be pure and in distinct parts, which is also sufficient. Selecting their two nonempty subsets gives sum_{i<j}(2^ni-1)(2^nj-1), while the one r=3 all-pure partition is triple-counted and needs subtraction by two. Four or more blocks force every block outside any coalition pair into one part and leave an impossible coalition partner; source proof covers these cases and the coalition-graph distinction. Independent brute-force adjacency-mask TOIDS/set-partition enumerations agreed for profiles (1,1,1),(2,1,1),(2,2,2),(3,2,1), including the reported (22,25) for K2,2,2. Finite enumeration corroborates only.
residual_risks: No classification for r=2 or arbitrary graphs; all claims require at least three nonempty parts.

value.rationale: All admissible partitions of a natural domination-coalition graph class are classified, and both nonzero coefficients and coalition graph types are explicit for arbitrarily many unequal labelled parts. A complete count of all witnesses refines the known scalar extremum in a motivated, reusable manner rather than merely recomputing its maximum or an arbitrary restricted slice.
residual_risks: The known value C=3 cannot be rebranded as the main novelty; its earlier proof and predicate are credited.

final_claim: For any finite complete r-partite graph r>=3 with labelled vertices and nonempty parts n_i, every valid total outer-independent coalition partition has exactly 2 or 3 nonempty blocks. Their unordered counts are c2=2^(N-1)-1-sum_i(2^ni-1) and c3=sum_{i<j}(2^ni-1)(2^nj-1)-2*[r=3], with sharp pure-block classification and exactly one triangular coalition graph for r=3.
